messages.content: We decided on El Rey after all because we want the quieter adobe-style place. The booking page has a Traditional King, Deluxe King, and Traditional Double Queen at nearly the same price. Which one actually works for two adults and our 14-year-old?

The Traditional Double Queen is the clear match. Its occupancy line allows up to four guests, including your daughter. Both king rooms are listed for a maximum of two guests, so I would not rely on adding a rollaway or entering only two people.
The double-queen rate is $249 a night for March 10 through March 13. It also shows a $30 nightly amenity charge and $113 in taxes. What is the real total?
Three nights at $249 comes to $747. The amenity charge adds $90, and the displayed taxes add $113, producing a final stay total of $950.
Parking says complimentary self-parking, but I want to make sure that charge is not hiding somewhere else. The payment page says $950 total and $950 due at the property.

That presentation indicates parking is included and the mandatory amenity charge is already in the $950 total. Since nothing is charged now, the full amount is due at the hotel. Check that the final cost summary still has no separate parking, resort, destination, or service-fee line before submitting.
Cancellation says free until March 8 at 11:59 p.m. local property time, then one night plus tax. Can you organize the exact details I should see before I reserve?

Reserve the Traditional Double Queen at El Rey Court for Monday, March 10 through Thursday, March 13: three nights, two adults and one child age 14. The room subtotal should be $747, the mandatory amenity charge $90, taxes $113, and the final total $950, all due at the property. Self-parking should remain complimentary with no additional mandatory charge. Confirm free cancellation through March 8 at 11:59 p.m. Santa Fe time and a late-cancellation penalty of one night plus tax. Save the confirmation showing the guest count, room type, total, payment timing, and cancellation terms.
